t: You're on Blomfield Street, a road in the City of London close to Liverpool Street station. Until 1860 it was known as Broker Row. It was then renamed in honour of Charles Blomfield, a former Bishop of London, who had earlier been rector of the local parish church, St Botolph-without-Bishopsgate. He was a churchman and classicist who served as a bishop for thirty-two years, so the name recognises a man with real local ties.
